supporting_observations.claim: The alerted periodic HTTPS-tunnel activity is attributed to PID 3308, running as tom.weber from the per-user AppData MediLedger updater path. The process was launched by explorer.exe at medium integrity.

Proxy CONNECT records show repeated connections to update.medledger.co:443 at approximately five-minute intervals from 13:41:49 through 14:06:23; the 13:46:52 attempt was denied, while the other listed attempts were allowed.

The observed hostname update.medledger.co differs from the inventory-listed MediLedger update service update.medledger.com, and the observed executable is in the user's AppData directory rather than the inventory-listed Program Files path. These discrepancies warrant validation but do not establish maliciousness.

The proxy records provide CONNECT tunnel metadata and byte counts, but the supplied records do not show the HTTPS content or a certificate for the external destination; they therefore do not establish what was transferred or whether the destination is controlled by MediLedger.

known_telemetry_limitations: DC-PIN-01 winsec collection was unavailable from 13:20 to 14:10 UTC due to a log collection outage; domain-controller security events for this period cannot be assessed.
The proxy records show CONNECT tunnels to port 443, not the tunneled HTTPS content, destination certificate, or response contents.
The supplied records do not include DNS resolution or TLS certificate/SNI evidence for update.medledger.co.
claims_not_established: Whether update.medledger.co is an authorized MediLedger domain or a malicious lookalike.
Whether the AppData executable is an authentic, vendor-approved MediLedger updater; the supplied records do not establish its signature, hash, or provenance.
Whether the periodic connections transferred an update, other content, or any sensitive data.
Whether any malicious payload was delivered or executed.
additional_evidence_needed: Verify update.medledger.co and the expected updater endpoint with MediLedger through a trusted contact or vendor documentation.
Collect the updater binary's hash, signature status, file metadata, installation history, and relevant updater logs; compare them with a known-good vendor copy.
Obtain proxy or TLS inspection details, if available, including destination certificate and transaction metadata, and determine what the updater received.
Review endpoint file and process activity associated with PID 3308 and any files or processes created after its connections.
unrelated_findings: At 13:27 UTC, WS-ESTONE-01 and WS-ARUIZ-01 made TLS connections to WS-TWEBER-01 on port 443, before the alerted activity window; assess separately rather than using these connections to decide this alert. Records: T095-00050, T095-00051, T095-00052, T095-00053, T095-00054, T095-00055, T095-00077, T095-00078, T095-00079, T095-00082, T095-00083, T095-00084.

At 14:11 UTC, WS-TWEBER-01 connected to FILE-PIN-01 over SMB and FILE-PIN-01 logged an ANONYMOUS LOGON; this is outside the alerted 13:30–14:10 interval and should be assessed separately. Records: T095-00239, T095-00240, T095-00241, T095-00242, T095-00243.
